newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: New U.N. chief believes Iraqi oil deal will work.
newsitem.headline: New U.N. chief believes Iraqi oil deal will work.

text.p: Kofi Annan, the U.N. secretary-general-elect, said on Wednesday he thought the oil-for-food deal with Iraq would go well.

Answering questions at his first news conference since he was appointed to the top job, Annan said, "My sense is that it will work. I think the Iraqi side will want to see it work and I would want to see it work."

The 58-year old Ghanaian head of peacekeeping operations, who takes up his five-year post on Jan. 1, said the credit for the Iraqi deal had to go to outgoing Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, who spent many hours during his term of office working on the plan.

It was implemented on Dec. 10 and allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy food and medicine for its people, suffering under sanctions imposed in August of 1990, when Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait.
Annan recalled that he led the first U.N. negotiating team with Iraq in 1991 when an earlier, similar plan was proposed by the U.N. Security Council but failed to materialise.
"I am happy for the Iraqi people, particularly the children, the needy in the society," he said.
